label: related
point: Affirmed dismissal of a gambling-currency forfeiture as time-barred under 19 U.S.C. 1621 because the five years ran from the Government's 1988 discovery of the offense, not from later offenses or seizure.
change: CAFRA added an alternative period for forfeitures: 2 years after discovery of the property's involvement in the offense, whichever is later.
why: The new alternative period addresses the same limitations rule, but the court found the Government knew by 1988 that bingo cash was being kept at the residence, so the property's involvement was also discovered then and the result would not change; the committee report names this decision only on the separate interest-award point.

label: unrelated
point: Denied a TRO, finding the Corps likely took into account effects on the White Farm under NHPA section 106 (16 U.S.C. 470f).
change: The section was repealed and recodified without substantive change as 54 U.S.C. 306108.
why: Pure recodification into title 54; the take-into-account duty is unchanged.

label: unrelated
point: Affirmed a continuing criminal enterprise conviction under 21 U.S.C. 848, finding sufficient evidence of supervising five or more persons and substantial income.
change: Repealed the CCE death-penalty procedure subsections (g)-(r), fixed a cross-reference, and added a methamphetamine kingpin provision.
why: The changes do not touch the CCE elements the decision applied.

label: unrelated
point: Cited 18 U.S.C. 1030 only to show the employee's charged computer offenses carried possible imprisonment, supporting the crime-provision suspension.
change: Broadened 1030 offenses (dropped interstate-communication element, restructured (a)(5), added extortion threats and conspiracy).
why: Passing citation; imprisonment remained available, and the decision did not construe the offense elements.

label: unrelated
point: Barred pre-petition habeas discovery for a capital prisoner; 848(q)(4)(B) and McFarland were discussed only in passing (mainly the concurrence) regarding pre-petition counsel.
change: Struck the 848(q) capital-appeal paragraphs and moved the counsel provisions to 18 U.S.C. 3599.
why: Relocation of the counsel provision; nothing changes the discovery rule the decision applied.

label: override_express
point: Held that 3729(a)(1) requires presentment to U.S. officers or employees (finding the evidence sufficient here), that (a)(2) has no presentment requirement, and that claims on CPA-administered non-appropriated funds were qualifying claims.
change: FERA removed the presentment-to-an-officer language from (a)(1), made (a)(2) turn on materiality, and broadened 'claim' to cover funds the Government provides or administers.
why: The court's (a)(1) presentment rule is eliminated and the report expressly responds to the Custer Battles litigation (on Iraqi funds administered by the U.S.); Congress's funds change agrees with this panel's result, so the override is on the presentment point.

label: related
point: Cited the ADA (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.) and affirmed summary judgment that a monocular worker was not regarded as substantially limited in working.
change: Rewrote the 12101 findings, removing the 43,000,000 figure and the 'discrete and insular minority' finding.
why: The findings changes belong to the ADAAA's rejection of narrow disability readings, but the decision relied on the 12102 definition rather than these findings; the changes that could alter its result are in 12102, not this block.

label: related
point: Dismissed a Chapter 7 case as a 'substantial abuse' under 707(b) on a totality-of-circumstances test, despite the statutory presumption favoring the debtor.
change: BAPCPA lowered the standard to 'abuse', removed the pro-debtor presumption, added a means test, and let any party in interest move.
why: Same subject, but the changes make dismissal easier and would not change this decision's result.

label: related
point: Held Rehabilitation Act section 501 claims use the ADA's 'because of' causation standard rather than section 504's 'solely by reason of', contrasting 12112(a)'s wording.
change: Changed 12112(a) from 'because of the disability of such individual' to 'on the basis of disability'.
why: The new phrase still lacks 'solely', so the decision's contrast and holding survive.

label: unrelated
point: Addressed the onset date for black lung benefits under the interim presumption, citing 921(c)(3) only to describe a Board case on the irrebuttable presumption.
change: Removed the sentence barring the 921(c)(4) fifteen-year presumption for post-1981 claims.
why: The (c)(4) change does not bear on the onset-date point the decision decided.

label: unrelated
point: Applied the trustee's 704(1) duty to collect estate property, holding that unjustified failure to pursue estate claims can be cause for removal.
change: Redesignated 704 as 704(a) and added new trustee duties and subsections.
why: Renumbering; the duty to collect and reduce to money is unchanged.

label: unrelated
point: Construed the Negotiated Rates Act's 10701(f)(9) small-business defense to undercharge claims (no election notice needed, defense may be raised late).
change: The ICC Termination Act rewrote 10701 as a rail-only provision and moved the motor-carrier undercharge provisions elsewhere.
why: Relocation and restructuring; the decision's small-business-defense point was not changed in substance.

label: unrelated
point: Affirmed denial of a 2255 motion without an evidentiary hearing on a right-to-testify ineffective-assistance claim.
change: Added subsection letters (a)-(h) to 2255's paragraphs.
why: Formal redesignation only.

label: unrelated
point: Held an ex-wife in contempt of the discharge injunction and awarded fees, citing 11 U.S.C. 101 et seq. only as the Code's general reference.
change: BAPCPA reworded the 101 definitions format and added new definitions.
why: Passing citation; the report names an unrelated 'Ray' case (In re C-L Cartage) on preference law.

label: related
point: Reversed summary judgment, holding a jury could find the officer actually or regarded as substantially limited in working a class of jobs; cited 12101 et seq. generally.
change: Rewrote the 12101 findings to undercut narrow disability readings.
why: Same subject, but the findings change only reinforces the broader coverage the decision already applied; its pro-plaintiff result would not change.

label: override_implicit
point: Following In re Amy, read 2259 as not limiting a child-pornography victim's losses to those proximately caused by the possessor, but vacated an unexplained $529,661 award.
change: The 2018 Act requires the court to find the victim's full losses and then order restitution reflecting the defendant's relative role in the causal process (minimum $3,000), with an aggregate cap.
why: The new text replaces the no-proximate-cause, full-losses approach the decision applied with a causation-based relative-role measure, but nothing in the packet shows Congress was responding to this decision.

label: codifies
point: Held innocent-spouse relief under 6013(e) may be apportioned, so a spouse who had reason to know of some understatement but not its magnitude can get partial relief.
change: RRA 1998 repealed 6013(e) and replaced it with new section 6015, which provides apportioned relief.
why: The committee report cites Wiksell approvingly for partial relief and the new statute writes apportionment in.

label: unrelated
point: Addressed whether 521(2) limits a debtor to surrender, redemption or reaffirmation, citing 522(f) only to note a purchase-money lien cannot be avoided.
change: Changed the judicial-lien exception to cross-reference 523(a)(5) and added a 'household goods' definition.
why: The 522(f) changes do not touch the purchase-money point or the 521(2) holding.

label: unrelated
point: Quoted the 704(1) duty of a Chapter 7 trustee to collect estate property in explaining why Chapter 7 debtors lose standing over prepetition claims.
change: Redesignated 704 as 704(a) and added duties.
why: Renumbering; the cited duty is unchanged.

label: related
point: Vacated a 3663 restitution order because the court failed to consider the defendant's ability to pay.
change: Restructured 3663(a), moving the financial-resources factors into (a)(1)(B), adding a victim definition, and excluding 3663A(c) offenses.
why: Ability to pay is still a required factor for 3663 orders; the mandatory-restitution carve-out comes from the 3663A regime rather than this law's changes to the point decided, so the effect on this decision's point is uncertain.

label: related
point: Rejected an equal protection challenge to 8418's survivor-annuity deposit, describing DOMA's 1 U.S.C. 7 definition and Windsor as background.
change: The Respect for Marriage Act replaced DOMA's man-woman definition with recognition of any valid marriage between 2 individuals.
why: Same subject (same-sex marriage), but the decision applied 8418, not section 7, and its holding does not depend on the old definition.

label: override_express
point: Held 'proceeds' in the money-laundering statutes means net profits rather than gross receipts (following Scialabba), and vacated the convictions.
change: FERA made 1957's 'proceeds' take the 1956 definition, which FERA added to cover gross receipts.
why: Congress reversed the profits reading, and the report says it is correcting the Supreme Court's Santos decision, which affirmed this decision.

label: unrelated
point: Cited NCLB (20 U.S.C. 6301 et seq.) only as background to the same-sex school regulations in a charter-renewal injunction case.
change: ESSA rewrote the Title I statement of purpose.
why: Passing citation with no relation to the decision's reasoning.
